motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Out-quad for feedback, colour, and release.

motion.name: ease-acquire
motion.purpose: Out-cubic for arrivals: brackets, corner marks, rings, the dial.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: In-out cubic for the theme iris and for rings turning back out; nothing snaps.

motion.name: control-feedback
motion.purpose: Shared control response and one-pixel press.

motion.name: lock-on
motion.value: brackets 340ms in (bottom pair +40ms), 260ms out; endpoint rings 700ms in, counter-rotating over 900ms
motion.purpose: Panels glide their brackets in; project endpoints dial their rings in around a centred, still arrow.

motion.name: corner-marks
motion.purpose: Small controls and the current navigation link; the reticle moves in place and never slides.

motion.name: theme-iris
motion.purpose: A theme change from the button opens from its centre; otherwise a 180ms crossfade; instant for reduced motion.

motion.name: dial-boot
motion.value: arcs draw 800ms with 60ms stagger; rings fade 700ms
motion.purpose: Once per visit, skipped on anchor or history arrival.

motion.name: readout-decode
motion.purpose: The only text scramble: the live readouts resolve as their data arrives, on an aria-hidden mask.

motion.name: scroll-linked
motion.value: section scale draws over cover 5%–30%; inner dial ring turns 45° as the hero leaves
motion.purpose: CSS scroll-driven animations; static where unsupported.

motion.name: header-hairline
motion.purpose: Confirms the sticky header is floating once the page has scrolled.

backdrops.name: sticky-header
backdrops.purpose: Separate pseudo-element layer keeps navigation readable and lets Safari tint from the page; opaque fallback.

display.purpose: Chakra Petch 600 in capitals: the name, section titles, and the dial's day.

body.purpose: IBM Plex Sans for titles (600), prose, and the About statement.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono for navigation, readouts, destinations, categories, days, genres, and handles.

japanese.purpose: System Japanese face at 13px, 500; decorative and aria-hidden.

components.name: Theme control
components.description: One tri-state button: each press advances Light to Dark to System; the glyph crossfades in place and a palette change opens as an iris from the button.
components.html: <button class="sample" type="button" aria-label="Color theme: Dark. Switch to System theme."><svg class="icon" width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 2.5a5 5 0 0 0 7.5 7.5 7.5 7.5 0 1 1-7.5-7.5Z"></path></svg></button>
components.css: .sample { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: #8ea6aa; cursor: pointer; transition: color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .sample:hover, .sample:focus-visible { color: #57d6ea; } .sample::before, .sample::after { position: absolute; content: ""; width: 7px; height: 7px; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .sample::before { inset: 0 auto auto 0; border-top: 1px solid #57d6ea; border-left: 1px solid #57d6ea; } .sample::after { inset: auto 0 0 auto; border-bottom: 1px solid #57d6ea; border-right: 1px solid #57d6ea; } .sample:hover::before, .sample:hover::after, .sample:focus-visible::before, .sample:focus-visible::after { opacity: 1; } .sample:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #57d6ea; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Project panel
components.description: A panel with one 12px cut corner; hover and focus lock on with three brackets while the endpoint rings spin in.
components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: grid; gap: 8px; padding: 20px; color: #d8e8ea; text-decoration: none; } .ds-panel::before { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; content: ""; background: #2a454c; clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 12px) 0, 100% 12px, 100% 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-panel::after { position: absolute; inset: 1px; z-index: -1; content: ""; background: #0d1c21; clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 11.41px) 0, 100% 11.41px, 100% 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-panel span { color: #f0ab4a; font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; }

components.name: Week dial
components.description: One turn is one week: 168 hour ticks, seven arcs from the schedule (weekdays amber, days off dashed, today cyan), a cyan now tick in Berlin time, and one inner ring that turns with scroll.
components.html: <svg class="ds-dial" viewBox="0 0 400 400" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="200" cy="200" r="190" /><path d="M204.19 40.05A160 160 0 0 1 322.44 97" /></svg>
components.css: .ds-dial { width: 240px; fill: none; } .ds-dial circle { stroke: #2a454c; } .ds-dial path { stroke: #f0ab4a; stroke-width: 3; }

narrative.northStar: A calm cyberbrain HUD over one person's work
narrative.overview: A project-first homepage in the Stand Alone Complex register: thin-line instruments, bilingual register labels, cyan for what you can act on, amber for what is recorded. The one bold object is a week dial built from the real schedule and the Berlin clock; everything else is quiet panels, a spec-sheet stack, and a duty-roster calendar. Motion answers the reader or runs once. Nothing is borrowed art or invented data.
keyCharacteristics: Two-signal palette: cyan for interaction and presence, amber for recorded data, no alarm red
A week dial built from the schedule and the Berlin clock
One cut corner, on project panels only, with lock-on brackets
Chakra Petch capitals, humanist body, monospace data, decorative Japanese sub-labels
Unnumbered content, always-visible navigation, no sliding indicators, no separators

researchInterpretation.summary: The dial, brackets, and bilingual labels are an original interpretation of Stand Alone Complex interface language: thin-line rings tied to a real target, dense real data on a strict grid, and short bilingual register labels. No franchise art, character, symbol, or on-screen text is reproduced, and no ring carries text around it or an emblem in its centre.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan means you can act here or this is now; amber means this is recorded. Every colour change is paired with a shape change.

rules.name: The No-Alarm Rule
rules.body: No red is defined because the page has no alert state.

rules.name: The One-Cut Rule
rules.body: Only project panels are chamfered; chips, cells, tags, and buttons stay square.

rules.name: The Answer-or-Once Rule
rules.body: Every movement answers the reader or runs once per visit; nothing loops.

rules.name: The One-Decode Rule
rules.body: Text scrambles only in the live readouts, on an aria-hidden mask; the real text never changes.

rules.name: The Real-Data Rule
rules.body: Every instrument measures something real: the schedule, the Berlin clock, the real destinations.

dos: Do keep every control at a 44px target and every action on cyan.
Do keep recorded data on amber and pair every colour change with a shape change.
Do build instruments from real data.
Do run bun test after any token change; the contrast test measures both themes.
Do honour reduced motion, forced colours, reduced transparency, more contrast, and no-JavaScript reading.
donts: Don't add section numbers, wide tracking, sliding indicators, separator lines, or a custom logo.
Don't chamfer anything but project panels, or glow anything but lines.
Don't scramble text anywhere but the live readouts, and never scramble Japanese.
Don't reproduce franchise art, marks, or on-screen text, or invent case numbers, timestamps, statuses, stamps, or redactions.
